seo.title: UI/UX & product design — Onedrag
seo.description: We design SaaS and web app interfaces in Figma — information architecture, dashboards, workflows and design systems — and hand off specs your developers build from.

hero.heading: We design software used every day.
hero.intro: We design SaaS and web app interfaces in Figma, build the design system behind them, and hand off specifications your developers work from. We do not build the product.

title: Information
architecture
points: Permissions and roles in the UI

title: Design
systems
points: Tokens for colour, type and spacing

title: Prototyping
points: Clickable flows for the real path
Prototypes you can test on users

title: New product
or MVP
items.description: You have a product to build and nothing drawn yet. We take it from flows to a design your developers can start on.

title: Redesign of an
existing product
items.description: The product works but has grown in every direction. We rework the structure and the screens without losing what your users already know.

title: Design system
build or cleanup
items.description: One set of components, tokens and rules, so screens stop drifting apart and a new one takes a day instead of a week.

title: Feature design for
an in-house team
items.description: You have designers and developers already. We take a feature or an area off their plate and work to the system you have.

title: Understand the
product and users
steps.description: We learn what the product does, who opens it every day, and what they are actually trying to finish. We read your support tickets and sit with the people who use it.

title: Map the flows
and structure
steps.description: We lay out the paths through the product and the shape of its navigation before any screen is drawn. Getting this wrong is expensive to fix later.

title: Design and
prototype in Figma
steps.description: Screens, states and components, assembled into a prototype you can click through. We design the edge cases too, not only the path where nothing goes wrong.

title: Hand off and
support the build
steps.description: Your developers get specs, component documentation and a system to work from. We stay reachable while they build and review what ships against the design.

items.question: Do you build it as well?
items.answer: No. We design in Figma and hand off to your developers — specs, component documentation, and answers while they build. We do build marketing sites in Framer, but that is a separate service; product front-ends we leave to your team.

items.question: What do we get at the end?
items.answer: A Figma file you own, with the screens, their states, and a component library behind them. Alongside it: a clickable prototype of the main flows, redlines and breakpoints, and written usage rules for the components.

items.question: Can you work inside our existing design system?
items.answer: Yes, and we prefer it when one exists. We design with your components and tokens, and tell you where a new one is genuinely needed rather than quietly adding variants. If the system has drifted, cleaning it up can be the engagement itself.

items.question: How do you price a project?
items.answer: On a call, once we know the scope. What it costs depends on where the product is — a new product, one that is growing, or a mature one that needs consistency across what is already built. There are no packages.

items.question: How do you work with our developers?
items.answer: They are in the process from the handoff step, and often earlier. We review what gets built against the design, answer questions in whatever channel your team already uses, and adjust the design when something turns out to be expensive to build.
